title: A walk can press the buttons in the Settings window
goal: Scripted checks can find buttons in the Settings window but pressing one does nothing, so nothing in Settings (Install for agents, deleting an Ask model, asking a silenced question again) can be proved by a walk the way a person clicks it.
notes: Reproduced 2026-10-26 on the probe (screen unlocked, Screen Recording granted, with and without setup front:true). Walk step: press "Agents Claude Code Install" -> log says in Install at window (460, 119), one click, the point is on the button in the -sc.png, but the button action never runs (a temporary NSLog at the top of AgentsSettingsSection.act never printed: /usr/bin/log show --last 2m --predicate eventMessage CONTAINS PZDEBUG was empty), and the next expect fails: no control called Agents Claude Code Uninstall. Two clicks (count 2) did nothing either; removing the row contextMenu and help did not change it. Scripts/playtest.sh Scripts/playtest/ask-deletes-an-older-model-walk.json --no-build passes, but its 2-delete-asks-sc.png shows no dialog after the press, so it never proved the press. The same buttons pressed through the accessibility tree (osascript, AXPress) worked at once. Press delivery: PlaytestHarness.swift around 8160-8215 (postEvent up, sendEvent down to the target window); panelWindows() includes the Settings window (around 7974). Suspect the synthetic mouse down into a non-key Settings window (SettingsWindowController hosts an NSHostingController in a plain NSWindow) is taken as a click to make it key.
acceptance: A walk pressing Install on the Claude Code row of Settings > Agents (with setup agentHome) sees the row change to Uninstall
The ask-deletes-an-older-model walk shows the Delete question after its press
agents-section-in-settings-walk presses Install and Uninstall on both rows and stays green

log.note: data point 2026-10-26: a posted press on a SWITCH in the Settings window does land. open-at-login-switch-in-settings-walk presses 'General Open at login' (window 472,336) and the expect after it reads off, then on again, and 2-open-at-login-off-sc.png shows it off. So the non-key-window theory does not cover toggles; whatever eats the click is specific to Buttons (or to the first press making the window key, then a toggle's mouse-up still flips it).
